It included an immediate 10% wage increase, boarding pay that boosts compensation by an average of 15% to 16%, retro pay, additional wage scale raises, scheduling improvements, increased flexibility and other improvements. Boarding pay, at a rate of 50% of regular pay, was to be added one year after the contract takes effect.
At American mainline, boarding pay was added six months after a contract with the Association of Professional Flight Attendants took effect.
It has become increasingly difficult for tentative deals on flight attendant contracts to be approved on the first attempt. On Friday, United Airlines and the AFA both said they were near agreement on a revised tentative agreement after members rejected a tentative agreement in July 2025. The United contract became amendable in August 2021.
At PSA, one flight attendant said Friday that the rejection appeared to reflect dissatisfaction with the proposed new pay scales and with the one-year delay in adding boarding pay, which has become the standard at mainline carriers.
